notes: Lyrics timing now reads the shape of the song first: the quiet stretches, the instrumental breaks and the long intro are measured from the recording and handed to the model as a map before it places a line.
A line that lands inside a measured instrumental stretch is moved to where the voice resumes, because nobody sings during a break, and a line that is already in the right place is left untouched.
When a song pauses, speeds up or changes tempo part-way through, the timing follows the recording rather than an even pace, so a verse after a break is no longer shifted by the part before it.
Songs that mix languages or scripts are timed line by line exactly as they are sung, without translating, dropping or merging a line.
The snap that pulls a line onto the nearest real rise in the song now ignores the instrumental frames, so a drum fill inside a break can never drag a lyric onto the drums.
The line count is still checked on every ask, and a short answer is requested again, which keeps one dropped line from shifting everything after it.
